citations.quote: For cortisol deficiency, a small daily dose of glucocorticoids is recommended.

Zycortal replaces the mineralocorticoid hormones only. Dogs with combined glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency should also receive a glucocorticoid such as prednisolone taking into account the current scientific knowledge.
Treatment should not be withdrawn suddenly
For use as replacement therapy for mineralocorticoid deficiency in dogs with primary hypoadrenocorticism (Addison’s disease).
Zycortal is intended for long term administration at intervals and doses dependent upon individual response.
The dose and the dosing interval are determined by electrolyte monitoring.
Once a stable dose and dosing interval are achieved, monthly DOCP injections may be administered by someone other than the veterinarian.
If DOCP cannot be used, consideration can be given to using fludrocortisone.
Re-evaluate the dog and measure the serum sodium/potassium ratio (Na⁺/K⁺ ratio) approximately 10 days after the first dose
Check electrolyte levels 10–14 days after injection and again 25 days after injection.

conflicts.conservativeDefault: Offer the day 10 and day 25 reminders after every injection, not only the first. The owner's vet sets the actual days.
conflicts.ownerWording: Published guidance differs slightly on the first test: about day 10 (product information) or days 10 to 14 (AAHA guidelines). Your vet's dates are used.

openQuestions: Crisis signs in words an owner would recognise. Both sources describe the crisis only as hypovolaemic shock, so crisisSigns is empty until a source lists owner-observable signs or the attesting vet approves specific wording.
Happening now for Addison's: no source gives thresholds, so it runs as a timer only.
Trend thresholds: no source gives any, so trends show numbers without judgement.
Whether owners should see a reference value for the Na:K ratio. The sources give values only for diagnosis or dose changes.
Whether the conservative default for monitoring (reminders after every injection) is right, or only while the dose is being set.
AAHA's 'routine biannual health care visits': confirm this means twice a year before adding a check-up reminder.
Fludrocortisone has no UK veterinary product; AAHA backs it only when DOCP cannot be used. Confirm it should appear for typical Addison's only.
Wording of the stress-plan prompt. The source sentence is addressed to vets and is never shown; the app asks the owner to agree a plan with their vet and shows the vet's own words.
Opened-vial alert: the source gives the 4-month limit only. Any earlier warning (for example 14 days before) has no source and is not included.
